card_quote: Default disposition (sceptic seed): price-led; buys Rs 150-300 Indian paperbacks or reads free content online; default answer to a foreign-priced fact book: no. / Myth exposure: knows science-history stories from school; Western pop-psychology and US history myths less familiar.
how_read: A few stories a night before sleeping, like scrolling fact pages. Did round 1 fully, most of round 2, and skimmed round 3. I also jumped ahead once to the cobra one because it said Delhi. Then exam prep took over and I didn't pick it up again that week.

w1_friction.note: I expected a quick reveal like on Instagram fact pages. The answer is one full page of text.
w1_friction.quote: The record separates the principle from the anecdote.

w1_friction.note: Newton's apple again? I just read this on the last page.
w1_friction.quote: Newton himself told of the apple, according to Britannica

w1_friction.note: Too much Latin. I skipped those lines and just read the end.
w1_friction.quote: Pluralitas non est ponenda sine necessitate

w1_friction.note: Never heard of Goodhart or this line, so I had nothing to guess with. British monetary policy, not exactly my thing.
w1_friction.quote: a paper on British monetary policy

w1_friction.note: Usenet and Godwin's law. Felt like an inside joke from old American internet.
w1_friction.quote: Godwin, an American attorney, coined the law

w1_friction.note: I didn't know who Kitty Genovese was, so how can I guess if the story is true or false? It assumes I've heard it.
w1_friction.quote: Kitty Genovese was murdered in 1964 while 38 people watched

w1_friction.note: A factory in Illinois and its lighting. Very dry, I skimmed it.
w1_friction.quote: a Western Electric factory in Cicero, Illinois

w1_friction.note: Two different numbers, a third and three-quarters, and I got confused which one is the point.
w1_friction.quote: Two numbers came out, and they are easy to confuse.

w1_best.why: It mentions the Sulba Sutras! We learned Pythagoras in school, never that India had it too. I'd post this one.
Einstein's Nobel for the photoelectric effect. Classic quiz question, now I know the exact citation.
Delhi cobras, and it actually traces to Madras. Nice to see India in the book, and the twist is good.
Blood, toil, tears and sweat. I also said blood, sweat and tears. Short and satisfying.
Archimedes and Eureka. Story we all know, and the Vitruvius bit was new.

w1_flat.why: Never heard of the original story, so the twist did nothing for me.
Didn't know Goodhart or the quote.
Old internet forum stuff, couldn't relate.
Latin and medieval friars. Too heavy.

w1_review.headline: Fun for quiz people, but very Western and long
w1_review.body: The science stories I knew from school, like Newton, Archimedes, Pythagoras and Einstein's Nobel, were fun to guess, and the Sulba Sutras and Delhi cobra mentions were a nice surprise. But many stories are American or British things I'd never heard of, so I couldn't even guess, and each answer is a full page when I wanted a quick reveal. Bottom line: good if it's cheap or a gift, otherwise I'd follow a quiz page for free.

w2_review_first: Yaar, ye ek quiz type book hai, har story pe guess karo true hai ya folklore. Newton, Einstein, Pythagoras wale mast hain, Sulba Sutras ka bhi mention hai. Par aadhi stories American hain, unka naam hi nahi suna, aur answers bahut lambe hain.

w2_lost.why: Round 2 mein Goodhart, Godwin, Sturgeon, ye log kaun hain? Kuch connect nahi hua, toh wahan se thoda bore ho gayi.
Kitty Genovese wali story pata hi nahi thi, toh guess karne ka maza nahi aaya.
Hawthorne factory wala, itna dry tha ki phone utha liya.
Asch wala itna lamba tha, wahan book band kar di aur phir exam prep shuru ho gaya.

w2_read_aloud.why: Delhi aur cobra, sab log interested honge, aur twist bhi hai ki story Madras ki thi.
Goldfish ki teen second memory sab ne suna hai, group mein sab argue karenge.
Garam paani pehle jamta hai ya nahi, ghar pe sab ka alag opinion hai, mazedaar fight hogi.
Einstein ka Nobel relativity ke liye nahi tha, ye quiz mein hamesha poochte hain.
Pythagoras se pehle Babylon aur India mein theorem tha, ye sun ke sab shock honge.

w2_cut.why: Domino theory, 1954 press conference, American politics hai, humein kya.
Nixon ki madman theory, ye bhi bahut American hai.
MAD acronym, Cold War ka topic, interest nahi aayega.
Harvard Business Review aur Conway, ye kaun hai pata hi nahi.
Overton window naam hi pehli baar suna, cut kar do.

w2_book2: Agar price 300 rupaye se upar hai aur phir se itni saari American stories hain, toh second book nahi lungi.
